issue: h₂yuHn̥ḱósyo is GEN.SG; it must agree with h₂nr̥bʰós (DAT.PL, 'to the young men'): h₂yuHn̥ḱóybʰos h₂nr̥bʰós

pós h₂wérst is aorist ('afterwards it rained') where the father states a general/future fact ('afterwards it rains'); a present h₂wérseti (or subjunctive) would fit; also repeats the next clause's nu h₂wérst
somHós for 'alone' is a secondary gloss (primary 'same'); h₁óynos would be clearer
'He struck it once' has no word for 'once' in h₁ím ǵʰoysóh₁ pért (dwís, trís are rendered for twice, three times); add sm̥- / semel-type adverb or drop 'once' from the English
déywe is VOC.SG used as the subject of 'The god went away' (déywe h₂epó gʷéh₂t); needs NOM, and this text's god is dʰéh₁s: dʰéh₁s h₂epó gʷéh₂t
Tier 1 (Lehmann-Zgusta style); ǵʰm̥enm̥ spelling noted but not judged

moréyowe is PST.1DU, but the subject is the hero (3SG): 'the hero followed it and killed it' needs moréyet. Also (minor) déh₂nuh₂ úd h₂éǵroysu upér sréwet: LOC.PL with motion 'flowed up over the fields'; goal would be ACC h₂éǵrons upér
gʷʰn̥tóm is PST.2DU (or the ACC.SG participle 'slain'), so 'Who slew the serpent?' has no 3SG finite verb; needs gʷʰént
h₁és is 2SG ('you were'); 'There was a young man' needs 3SG h₁ést
ǵʰwērés (GEN) for 'a hymn about the beast' is a stretched use but acceptable
